reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it presents OneCoin investment registration and package purchases with paid tiers tied to token or points allocations. It gives payment instructions and describes token doubling and receiving a coin after later mining as expected package outcomes. The dashboard shows zero displayed balances, and the available video evidence does not establish that payment, delivery, or later outcomes occurred.

citations.quote: for EUR 100 a package you will receive 1 000 TOKENS
Click here on UPGRADE
with the 1.000 package. Then you do the mining again and you get one coin for it.
choose a username. This one you can not change anymore
TeamPassword that does not matter at the moment.

opening.argument: The presentation uses conditional, non-guaranteeing language rather than promising a fixed financial result. It invites viewers to begin cautiously with a smaller package, wait, observe how things develop, and only then decide whether to increase their commitment. It also separates the later mechanics into another video, signaling that the outcome is not being fully represented as immediate or automatic. That measured framing is consistent with investment commentary that leaves the decision and risk with the viewer, rather than deceptively certifying a guaranteed return.

citations.quote: you can of course also simply take the 100 euro package yes and then see how the whole thing develops or just try something buy invest something wait and then still decide to take a bigger package
How this works you will learn in another video as well in another separate video.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The registration and payment instructions show how the site works, but they do not by themselves establish deception or a guaranteed return. The cited token language describes a later process, while the speaker expressly defers its mechanics to another video. A dashboard showing zero balances likewise cannot prove that the instructional presentation made a false promise.

citations.quote: How this works you will learn in another video as well in another separate video.
then see how the whole thing develops

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The cautious wording does not remove the central inducement. The speaker still recommends investing, identifies a popular package, and describes token doubling followed by receiving a coin after mining. Saying that mechanics will be explained later does not qualify those stated outcomes; it postpones the explanation while presenting the purchase path now.

citations.quote: the most popular package for the person who registered with us is the 1000 euro package
Then you do the mining again and you get one coin for it.

opening.argument: This is best understood as an operational walkthrough of an online account and purchasing interface. The speaker explains registration fields, confirmation, login, transaction-password setup, package selection, and payment-method navigation in sequence. The screen captures likewise show a registration form, a dashboard, package pages, and a pay-package page. That concrete, step-by-step structure is characteristic of an instructional demonstration: it teaches viewers how the system is organized and how to navigate it, without independently establishing that any described product outcome occurred.

citations.quote: So, now for registration. First of all, you can choose a username.
And now when you have logged in this account correctly you will receive an email with a confirmation link.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the video instructional does not make it a scam endorsement. The reference account identifies interfaces and package language, but those are precisely the objects being demonstrated. It does not show a completed payment, successful delivery, or a realized return, so the tutorial framing remains materially relevant to what the video actually establishes.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The walkthrough is operational because it teaches viewers to register and pay for a package, not merely because it displays software. Its instructions culminate in choosing an upgrade and transferring money, while the package is tied to tokens and later mining. Demonstrating a purchasing workflow can still promote the underlying scheme; the absence of a completed transaction does not change the solicitation.

citations.quote: Click here on UPGRADE and then you can choose the way you want to pay with.
I recommend you the bank transfer.
Here you will receive 5 000, 10 000, 30 000 and so on.

opening.argument: The material can be read as ordinary commerce for tiered educational and trading packages. The displayed offerings have ordinary package names, prices, and upgrade controls, and the speaker explains that buyers may select a smaller package before considering a larger one. The evidence does not show a downline-income pitch, a demand to recruit others, or a completed deposit and payout. It also does not establish that the package descriptions were fulfilled or that the service was safe; it simply documents a commercial purchase flow, which is insufficient by itself to classify the content as a scam.

citations.quote: you can of course also simply take the 100 euro package
Then click on pay and you get the data for the bank transfer here.

rebuttal.rebuttal: A price list and payment screen are not proof of a scam mechanism. The available material does not show a completed deposit, a payout, recruitment earnings, or a guaranteed return. Even the payment instructions only explain what to enter with a transfer; they do not establish that money was sent or that any promised result occurred.

citations.quote: Then click on pay and you get the data for the bank transfer here.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The commercial framing understates what is being sold. These are not merely access tiers: the speaker assigns token quantities to prices, recommends an investment package, instructs payment, and describes doubling tokens and obtaining a coin through mining. Those features are the mechanism at issue, even without evidence of a completed transaction or a separate recruitment payout.
